verdicts.reason: A just keeps the original elements at banner size on a taller canvas. The headline and subline are split by a big empty gap, so the copy no longer reads as one group. The logo and the text are tiny and leave a lot of dead space above and below them. B scales everything up and keeps the headline and subline together, with the CTA on the right. But its Quillbrook logo is oversized: it competes with the headline and nearly touches the top and bottom edges, and the left margin is tight.
